text.p: BankAmerica Corp's new global retail-banking president sees acquisition opportunities for the nation's third-largest bank in the consolidating California market and outside the United States.

"There are going to be opportunities on the acquisition side. Management and the board want to grow their franchise profitably," Eugene Lockhart said on Wednesday. He said it was too early to be specific about possible acquisitions.
Lockhart, 47, had served as president and chief executive officer of MasterCard International since 1994.

Lockhart's appointment is seen by analysts as a key move by Chief Executive David Coulter, who has a wholesale banking background. Coulter announced a sweeping restructuring in December, including elimination of 3,700 jobs worldwide.

"BankAmerica needed a strong retail leader, and they came up with Lockhart, who by virtue of his last two jobs, is a heavyweight in retail with a strong emphasis on technology," said Ray Soifer, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.
Lockhart's appointment also comes at a time when BankAmerica faces heated competition overseas, particularly from the second-largest U.S. bank, Citibank, analysts said.

"Citibank is very far ahead on technology for global retail banking, particularly in the Far East. BankAmerica is really playing catchup, and this appointment is a big step for Bankamerica," said Charlotte Chamberlain of Jefferies & Co.
Lockhart plans to focus on Asia. "There's a lot of opportunities in the Pacific Rim to grow. We'll go into some new countries and deeper into the countries we already have a presence," he said.
Chief Executive Coulter said Lockhart was especially adept at guiding financial services businesses through technological change.
